name: Point
description: Places a single point object at a picked or typed location. Useful for marking setting-out positions, snap targets and survey coordinates before drawing geometry.

name: Points
description: Places a run of point objects one after another until you press Enter. Quicker than repeating Point when plotting several markers or imported coordinate positions.

name: PointCloud
description: Gathers selected point objects into a single point cloud, or breaks a cloud back into points. Keeps large scan or survey datasets manageable as one selectable object.

name: Line
description: Draws a single straight line between two picked points. The most basic drafting tool, used constantly for construction lines, edges and setting-out geometry.

name: Polyline
description: Draws a connected chain of straight segments as one curve. Ideal for plan outlines, boundaries and any profile made of straight runs.

name: Curve
description: Draws a free-form NURBS curve by placing control points that pull the curve towards them. The go-to tool for smooth, editable design curves where flow matters more than hitting exact points.

name: InterpCrv
description: Draws a smooth curve that passes exactly through each picked point. Reach for it when tracing site outlines, sections or scanned drawings where the curve must hit known positions.

name: InterpCrvOnSrf
description: Draws an interpolated curve that lies directly on a surface, following its curvature between picked points. Useful for laying out seams, panel joints or path lines across doubly curved forms.

name: Sketch
description: Draws a freehand curve that follows the dragged cursor, optionally on a surface or mesh. Handy for loose concept lines and annotating models during design reviews.

name: Arc
description: Draws a circular arc from a centre, start and angle, with options for tangent and other constructions. Everyday tool for door swings, filleted corners drawn manually and curved wall segments.

name: Arc3Pt
description: Draws an arc through three picked points. Quick when you know where the arc starts, ends and passes, but not its centre or radius.

name: Circle
description: Draws a circle from centre and radius, with vertical, tangent and other placement options. Fundamental for columns, service penetrations and construction geometry.

name: Circle3Pt
description: Draws a circle through three picked points. Useful for reconstructing circles from surveyed or traced positions where the centre is unknown.

name: Ellipse
description: Draws an ellipse from a centre and two axis lengths, or by bounding corners. Used for elliptical plans, arches and lighting layouts.

name: Rectangle
description: Draws a rectangular polyline from two corners, a centre, or three points, with a rounded-corner option. The starting point for most plan footprints and panel outlines.

name: Polygon
description: Draws a regular polygon with any number of sides, inscribed or circumscribed about a radius. Handy for bolt patterns, kiosks and faceted plan forms.

name: Helix
description: Draws a 3D helix around an axis with a set number of turns and pitch. The base curve for spiral stairs, coiled details and threaded forms.

name: Spiral
description: Draws a flat or conical spiral with controllable turns and radii. Useful for ramps, spiral geometry studies and decorative patterns.

name: Conic
description: Draws a conic section curve controlled by end points, a shoulder and a rho value. Valued in industrial and facade design for tight, mathematically clean transition curves.

name: Parabola
description: Draws a parabola from focus or vertex definitions. Occasionally needed for reflector geometry, arch profiles and structural form studies.

name: Hyperbola
description: Draws a hyperbola from focus and vertex parameters. A niche precision curve for shell structures and reflector studies.

name: Fillet
description: Joins two curves with a tangent arc of a given radius, trimming them back to meet it. The standard way to round corners in plans and profiles.

name: Chamfer
description: Connects two curves with an angled straight segment at set distances, trimming them to suit. Used for bevelled corners on frames, plates and joinery profiles.

name: FilletCorners
description: Rounds every corner of a polyline or polycurve with one radius in a single operation. Saves picking corner pairs one by one on panel outlines and plan shapes.

name: BlendCrv
description: Creates an adjustable smooth connecting curve between two curve ends, with control over continuity up to curvature and beyond. Reach for it when a plain fillet looks too mechanical.

name: ArcBlend
description: Bridges two curves with a pair of tangent arcs you can adjust interactively. A quick alternative to BlendCrv when arc-based geometry is preferred for fabrication.

name: Connect
description: Extends or trims two curves so their ends meet exactly. Fast tidy-up for drafting where lines overshoot or fall short of a corner.

name: Extend
description: Lengthens a curve to meet a boundary or by a set distance, keeping its character by line, arc or smooth continuation. Constantly used to make curves reach trimming edges.

name: Offset
description: Creates a parallel copy of a curve at a set distance, with corner and cap options. The backbone of wall thicknesses, clearance zones and repeated profile lines.

name: OffsetCrvOnSrf
description: Offsets a curve that lies on a surface so the copy stays on the surface at a true geodesic-style distance. Used for setting out seams and edge details on curved facades.

name: Fair
description: Gently re-smooths a curve to remove kinks and wobbles in its curvature while keeping close to its original shape. Used on imported or traced curves before building quality surfaces from them.

name: Smooth
description: Averages out control point positions to relax curves, surfaces or meshes, with per-axis control. Good for calming noisy traced linework or lumpy meshes.

name: SimplifyCrv
description: Replaces segments of a polycurve with true lines and arcs where possible, reducing clutter. Excellent for cleaning up curves imported from CAD drawings.

name: Match
description: Adjusts the end of one curve to meet another with position, tangency or curvature continuity. Essential prep before lofting or sweeping surfaces that must flow together.

name: MakePeriodic
description: Converts a closed curve or surface so it has no kink at its seam, making it smoothly continuous all the way round. Useful before building smooth closed lofts or revolves.

name: CloseCrv
description: Closes an open curve either with a straight segment or by adjusting the curve to meet itself. Needed before extruding or building planar surfaces that require closed boundaries.

name: CrvSeam
description: Moves the seam point of a closed curve to a new position along it. Fixes twisting in lofts and sweeps caused by mismatched seam locations between profiles.

name: InsertKnot
description: Adds a knot to a curve or surface, creating extra control points at that parameter without changing the shape. Gives finer local editing control exactly where you need it.

name: RemoveKnot
description: Deletes a knot from a curve or surface, simplifying its control structure with a slight shape change. Used to lighten over-detailed geometry before matching or exporting.

name: FitCrv
description: Refits a curve to a given tolerance with fewer control points. A quick way to tame dense curves from tracing, intersections or imported data.

name: SoftEditCrv
description: Drags a point on a curve while nearby regions follow with a smooth falloff. Ideal for nudging long design curves without introducing kinks or editing individual control points.

name: TweenCurves
description: Generates intermediate curves evenly blended between two input curves. Great for louvre arrays, contour infills and transitional profiles between two design conditions.

name: CurveThroughPt
description: Builds a single curve through a set of selected point objects in order. Turns imported survey or grid points into usable design curves in one step.

name: Divide
description: Places point objects along a curve by equal count or set length. The standard setting-out tool for mullion spacing, baluster positions and panelisation.

name: Project
description: Projects curves or points straight down (or along a view direction) onto surfaces, polysurfaces or meshes. Used to push plan linework onto terrain or facade geometry.

name: Pull
description: Pulls curves or points onto a surface by the shortest path rather than a fixed direction. Better than Project on steep or doubly curved surfaces where projection would distort placement.

name: Contour
description: Cuts a stack of evenly spaced section curves through objects along an axis. The classic tool for site contours, waffle structures and laser-cut sectional models.

name: Section
description: Creates section curves where a picked plane slices through objects. Quick one-off cuts for studying profiles or extracting a single section line for drawings.

name: Silhouette
description: Extracts outline curves of objects as seen from the current view or a set direction. Useful for shadow studies, elevational outlines and preparing artwork from 3D models.

name: Intersect
description: Creates curves or points where selected objects cross each other. Used constantly to find true junction lines between roofs, walls and complex surfaces.

name: DupBorder
description: Duplicates the naked outer edges of a surface, polysurface, mesh or hatch as curves. Fast way to recover an outline for offsetting, trimming or documentation.

name: DupEdge
description: Copies individually picked surface or polysurface edges as free-standing curves. Handy for rebuilding, sweeping or dimensioning from existing geometry.

name: DupFaceBorder
description: Duplicates the full border of a chosen face within a polysurface, including any trim holes. Useful when detailing a single panel of a larger assembly.

name: ExtractIsocurve
description: Pulls a chosen U or V isocurve off a surface as a real curve. Used to harvest clean construction curves that follow a surface's natural flow.

name: ExtractWireframe
description: Converts the displayed isocurve wireframe of surfaces or polysurfaces into curves in one go. Quick source of a full curve network for diagrams and pattern studies.

name: CreateUVCrv
description: Lays out a surface's border and trim curves flat in world XY according to its UV parameter space. The first step for designing perforation or graphic patterns that will be flowed back onto the surface.

name: CurveBoolean
description: Trims and joins overlapping closed planar curves by picking the regions to keep, like a 2D boolean. Brilliant for cleaning up overlapping plan outlines into single boundaries.

name: EndBulge
description: Adjusts how strongly a curve or surface end holds its shape near a matched edge without breaking continuity. A fine-tuning tool used after Match or MatchSrf.

name: Loft
description: Fits a surface through an ordered series of profile curves, with style options from tight to loose. A staple for canopies, hulls and any form defined by cross-sections.

name: Sweep1
description: Runs one or more cross-section shapes along a single rail curve to build a surface. Ideal for handrails, mouldings and extrusion-like forms that follow a curved path.

name: Sweep2
description: Builds a surface by carrying cross-sections along two rail curves, keeping both edges under control. The tool of choice when a shape must hit two defined boundary curves.

name: Revolve
description: Spins a profile curve around an axis to create a surface of revolution. The fastest route to domes, columns, bowls and other rotationally symmetrical forms.

name: RailRevolve
description: Revolves a profile around an axis while its outer edge follows a rail curve, so the radius varies as it turns. Useful for shells and vault-like forms that are not purely circular in plan.

name: NetworkSrf
description: Builds a surface through a criss-crossing network of curves in two directions. Powerful for complex freeform patches where lofts and sweeps cannot capture the shape.

name: Patch
description: Fits an approximate surface over a loose collection of curves, points or edges. A pragmatic hole-filler and terrain-builder when inputs are messy or incomplete.

name: PlanarSrf
description: Creates flat surfaces from closed planar curves, including nested boundaries with holes. Everyday tool for turning plan outlines into floor plates and panels.

name: SrfPt
description: Creates a surface by picking three or four corner points. Quick for simple planes and twisted quads such as warped roof panels.

name: EdgeSrf
description: Builds a surface spanning two, three or four boundary curves or edges. A dependable way to skin simple openings and quad patches without loft direction fuss.

name: ExtrudeCrv
description: Pushes a curve in a straight direction to form a surface, or a closed solid with caps. The workhorse for turning plans into walls and profiles into massing.

name: ExtrudeCrvAlongCrv
description: Extrudes a profile curve along the length of another curve, keeping the profile orientation fixed. Useful for angled glazing bars and raked structural members where a sweep would rotate the section.

name: ExtrudeCrvToPoint
description: Extrudes a curve so it tapers to a single apex point. Instant tool for pyramidal roofs, spires and cone-like transitions from any plan shape.

name: ExtrudeCrvTapered
description: Extrudes a curve with a draft angle so the sides lean in or out as they rise. Used for battered walls, formwork with draft and tapered massing studies.

name: OffsetSrf
description: Creates a copy of a surface or polysurface at a set distance along its normals, optionally building a closed solid between the two. The standard way to give architectural surfaces material thickness.

name: VariableOffsetSrf
description: Offsets a surface with different distances at chosen points, blending smoothly between them. Useful when a shell or panel must thicken structurally in some zones only.

name: BlendSrf
description: Creates a smooth transition surface between two surface edges with adjustable continuity and shape handles. The refined option for junctions where FilletSrf feels too rigid.

name: ChamferSrf
description: Connects two surfaces with a flat angled strip at set distances, trimming both back. Suits bevelled edges on plinths, frames and machined-looking details.

name: FilletSrf
description: Inserts a constant-radius rounded surface between two surfaces and can trim them to fit. Used for radiused junctions between individual surfaces rather than solid edges.

name: MatchSrf
description: Adjusts a surface edge to meet a neighbouring surface with position, tangency or curvature continuity. The key tool for achieving seamless multi-patch surfaces in high-quality modelling.

name: MergeSrf
description: Combines two untrimmed surfaces sharing an edge into one single surface. Useful for simplifying models before offsetting, unrolling or exporting.

name: Drape
description: Drops a rectangular surface over objects from above, like laying cloth across the model. A quick way to make simplified terrain or wrapper surfaces over complex geometry.

name: Heightfield
description: Generates a relief surface or mesh from the light and dark values of an image. Handy for quick terrain from greyscale maps and textured feature walls.

name: PlaneThroughPt
description: Fits a rectangular plane through a set of points, averaging their positions. Useful for establishing a best-fit datum through surveyed or scanned data.

name: CutPlane
description: Creates flat planes that slice through selected objects at picked locations, sized to cover them. Convenient starting geometry for trimming solids or setting up section cuts.

name: UnrollSrf
description: Flattens developable (single-curvature) surfaces onto a plane, with their marked curves and labels. Essential for fabrication drawings of sheet metal, timber veneers and curved cladding.

name: Squish
description: Flattens doubly curved surfaces or meshes by allowing controlled stretching and compression, and can report the distortion. Used to pattern fabric panels, upholstery and stretch ceilings.

name: Smash
description: Roughly flattens a surface that is only slightly doubly curved, ignoring small distortions. A quick-and-dirty alternative to Squish for near-developable panels.

name: ShrinkTrimmedSrf
description: Shrinks the hidden underlying surface of a trimmed face so it sits closely around the trim boundary. Good housekeeping before matching, exporting or editing control points.

name: Untrim
description: Removes a trim boundary and restores the full underlying surface, optionally keeping the trimming curves. Used to recover clean geometry when a trim needs rethinking.

name: ExtendSrf
description: Lengthens a surface beyond a chosen edge, smoothly or as a straight continuation. Handy when a roof or wall surface falls just short of the geometry it must trim against.

name: SoftEditSrf
description: Drags a point on a surface with a smooth circular falloff so the surrounding region follows naturally. Ideal for sculpting gentle bumps and hollows into terrain or shell forms.

name: MoveUVN
description: Nudges control points along a surface's U, V and normal directions with sliders and smoothing. A precise sculpting panel for refining surface interiors without breaking edges.

name: RebuildUV
description: Rebuilds a surface in just the U or V direction with a chosen point count. Useful for evening out isocurve distribution in one direction while leaving the other intact.

name: DivideAlongCreases
description: Splits a surface into separate faces wherever it kinks at tangency or curvature breaks. Cleans up geometry so downstream fillets, offsets and exports behave predictably.

name: SrfSeam
description: Relocates the seam of a closed surface to a different isocurve position. Fixes texture, trim and matching issues that cluster around a badly placed seam.

name: Box
description: Creates a rectangular solid box from corners or centre. The first tool most designers reach for in massing studies and quick spatial blocking.

name: Sphere
description: Creates a solid sphere from centre and radius or other constructions. Used for domes, finials and quick volumetric placeholders.

name: Cylinder
description: Creates a solid cylinder from a base circle and height. Everyday geometry for columns, pipework and circular cores.

name: Cone
description: Creates a solid cone from a base and apex. Useful for roof forms, funnels and transitional volumes.

name: TCone
description: Creates a truncated cone between two circular ends of different radii. Handy for tapered columns, hoppers and flared connections.

name: Torus
description: Creates a solid ring from a centre, ring radius and tube radius. Occasionally needed for handrail loops, gaskets and toroidal architectural forms.

name: Ellipsoid
description: Creates a solid ellipsoid stretched along three axes. Useful for blob-like massing and organic volume placeholders.

name: Pyramid
description: Creates a solid pyramid with any number of base sides. Instant geometry for pyramidal roofs, skylights and obelisks.

name: Tube
description: Creates a hollow straight cylinder with wall thickness in one operation. Quicker than boolean-subtracting two cylinders for sleeves and ducts.

name: Pipe
description: Wraps a solid circular section along any curve, with optional varying radii and caps. The fastest way to model handrails, service runs and structural tubes.

name: Slab
description: Offsets a planar curve and extrudes the result into a solid with thickness and height in one step. A quick way to raise walls from single plan lines.

name: ExtrudeSrf
description: Thickens a surface by extruding it straight into a closed solid. Used to give floor plates and panels physical depth for booleans and sections.

name: ExtrudeSrfTapered
description: Extrudes a surface with a draft angle so its sides slope as they rise. Useful for foundations, moulds and casting geometry needing release angles.

name: BooleanUnion
description: Merges overlapping solids into one, removing internal walls. The standard way to consolidate massing elements into a single clean volume.

name: BooleanDifference
description: Subtracts one set of solids from another, cutting openings and voids. Constantly used for door and window openings, service penetrations and courtyard cuts.

name: BooleanIntersection
description: Keeps only the volume shared by two sets of solids. Useful for finding overlap zones, clash volumes and sculpting forms from intersecting masses.

name: BooleanSplit
description: Splits solids into separate closed pieces along their shared intersections, keeping everything. Great for dividing a massing model into phases or storeys while retaining all parts.

name: Boolean2Objects
description: Cycles interactively through all boolean outcomes of two objects until you see the one you want. A forgiving way to run booleans without remembering which operand order to pick.

name: Cap
description: Closes planar openings in a surface or polysurface with flat faces, making it a closed solid. The usual fix after extruding or trimming leaves an open top or bottom.

name: ExtractSrf
description: Separates chosen faces from a polysurface so they become independent surfaces, leaving the rest behind. Used to isolate a facade panel or roof face for detailed work.

name: Shell
description: Hollows a closed solid to a set wall thickness, removing the faces you pick as openings. Ideal for turning massing volumes into thin-walled enclosures in one move.

name: FilletEdge
description: Rounds selected edges of a solid with constant or variable radii, handling the corner patches automatically. The standard finishing tool for softening built edges before rendering or fabrication.

name: ChamferEdge
description: Bevels selected solid edges with a flat strip at set distances. Used for arris details, machined looks and edge easing on precast elements.

name: BlendEdge
description: Rounds solid edges with a curvature-continuous blend rather than a plain circular fillet. Chosen when reflections must flow uninterrupted across an edge, as on visible ceiling or furniture pieces.

name: MoveFace
description: Pushes or pulls a face of a solid, extending the neighbouring faces to follow. Quick parametric-feeling edits like making a box taller or a recess deeper without remodelling.

name: MoveEdge
description: Moves a single edge of a solid while the connected faces stretch to keep the body closed. Useful for tweaking wedge angles and ridge lines directly.

name: MoveHole
description: Slides an existing hole to a new position within its planar face. Saves re-cutting openings when a penetration needs repositioning.

name: RoundHole
description: Cuts a circular hole into a solid at a picked point, with depth and direction options. Faster than drawing a cylinder and boolean-subtracting for fixings and service penetrations.

name: MakeHole
description: Cuts a hole through a solid using a closed profile curve you supply. The general-purpose opening cutter for shaped penetrations and window reveals.

name: ArrayHole
description: Repeats an existing hole across a face in rows and columns. Efficient for perforated panels and fixing grids once one opening is placed.

name: WireCut
description: Slices a solid using a curve projected through it, keeping or discarding the pieces you choose. An intuitive cutter for stepped facades and profile-driven subtractions.

name: SplitFace
description: Divides a planar face of a solid along a curve or between points without breaking the solid apart. Sets up sub-faces that MoveFace or PushPull can then manipulate independently.

name: MergeAllCoplanarFaces
description: Dissolves unnecessary edges between flat faces that lie in the same plane. Tidies solids after booleans so they read cleanly and export with fewer faces.

name: CreateSolid
description: Builds closed solids from a set of intersecting surfaces that enclose volumes. Useful late in a workflow when separate walls, roofs and cuts need consolidating into watertight bodies.

name: PushPull
description: Drags planar regions directly in or out to add or remove material, SketchUp-style. Introduced in Rhino 8, it makes fast massing edits without explicit boolean commands.

name: Inset
description: Creates a smaller face inside a chosen face at a set margin, ready to push or pull. Added in Rhino 8, it pairs with PushPull for panelled and recessed detailing.

name: SolidPtOn
description: Turns on grip points at the corners and edges of a solid so they can be dragged directly. A light-touch way to deform boxes and simple polysurfaces without exploding them.

name: SubDBox
description: Creates a SubD box with a chosen number of faces per side. A common starting block for organic massing that will be sculpted by pushing points and edges.

name: SubDSphere
description: Creates a smooth SubD sphere built from quad faces. Useful as a base for organic forms like pods, boulders and soft furniture.

name: SubDCylinder
description: Creates a SubD cylinder with configurable face counts. A clean starting point for soft columns, trunks and limb-like forms.

name: SubDCone
description: Creates a SubD cone primitive for sculpting tapered organic shapes. Handy for tent-like and horn-like starting volumes.

name: SubDTorus
description: Creates a SubD ring primitive. A useful base for smooth loops, seating rings and continuous banded forms.

name: SubDPlane
description: Creates a flat SubD plane divided into a grid of faces. The usual canvas for sculpting terrain-like or draped SubD surfaces.

name: ToSubD
description: Converts meshes, NURBS surfaces or extrusions into SubD objects. The gateway for bringing existing geometry into Rhino's smooth sculpting workflow.

name: ToNURBS
description: Converts SubD or mesh objects into NURBS surfaces and polysurfaces. Used when a sculpted concept needs precise trimming, filleting or export to documentation.

name: QuadRemesh
description: Rebuilds any mesh, surface or SubD as a clean quad-dominant mesh, optionally converting straight to SubD. Transforms scan data and faceted models into sculptable, well-flowing geometry.

name: MultiPipe
description: Builds a smooth SubD pipe network over a set of connected curves, resolving the junctions automatically. Perfect for branching structures, node details and tubular furniture frames.

name: Bridge
description: Connects two SubD or mesh face groups or edge loops with a smooth linking tunnel. Used to join limbs, create handles and punch connected openings through sculpted forms.

name: Stitch
description: Zips selected SubD or mesh edges together so they become shared edges. The tool for closing gaps and welding sculpted parts into one continuous body.

name: AppendFace
description: Adds new faces onto existing SubD or mesh edges by picking corner points. Used to grow a form outwards face by face during freeform modelling.

name: SingleSubDFace
description: Creates one standalone SubD face from picked corner points. The seed for box-modelling a form face by face with AppendFace.

name: InsertEdge
description: Adds new edge loops across SubD faces to tighten or add detail in a region. The main way to control how crisp or soft a sculpted feature reads.

name: InsertPoint
description: Adds vertices along SubD edges, splitting the neighbouring faces. Fine-grained alternative to InsertEdge when only part of a loop needs extra control.

name: Subdivide
description: Splits selected SubD or mesh faces into smaller faces for denser local control. Used when one area of a sculpt needs much finer modelling than the rest.

name: Bevel
description: Replaces selected SubD edges or vertices with narrow face strips, hardening the corner while staying smooth. The SubD equivalent of a fillet for controlling edge tightness.

name: Crease
description: Makes selected SubD edges or vertices perfectly sharp while the rest stays smooth. Essential for mixing crisp architectural arrises into otherwise soft forms.

name: RemoveCrease
description: Returns creased SubD edges or vertices to smooth. Used when a hard edge should melt back into the surrounding form.

name: Reflect
description: Maintains a live mirrored half of a SubD so edits on one side update the other instantly. Invaluable for symmetrical furniture, vehicles and pavilion forms.

name: Radiate
description: Applies live radial symmetry to a SubD so edits repeat around an axis. Added in Rhino 8 for rotationally patterned objects like lighting pieces and radial pavilions.

name: OffsetSubD
description: Offsets a SubD inwards or outwards, optionally building a closed solid shell between the two. The standard way to give sculpted skins a real material thickness.

name: MergeFaces
description: Combines adjacent SubD or mesh faces into a single larger face. Used to simplify topology after heavy editing.

name: SubDLoft
description: Lofts a series of profile curves into a SubD surface with clean quad flow. A Rhino 8 addition for building smooth sculptable skins straight from section curves.

name: SubDSweep1
description: Sweeps profiles along one rail to produce a SubD rather than a NURBS surface. Keeps concept geometry light and editable for further sculpting.

name: SubDSweep2
description: Sweeps profiles along two rails to build a SubD skin controlled at both edges. Useful for organic canopies and seat shells that need later point editing.

name: SubDDisplayToggle
description: Switches SubD display between smooth and flat (boxy control cage) modes. Designers flip to flat mode for precise topology edits, then back to judge the smooth result.

name: Mesh
description: Converts NURBS surfaces, polysurfaces or SubD into a polygon mesh with density controls. Used before 3D printing, export to game engines or heavy visualisation scenes.

name: MeshBox
description: Creates a box directly as a mesh with set face counts. Useful for lightweight massing in mesh-based workflows and export pipelines.

name: MeshSphere
description: Creates a sphere as a polygon mesh with controllable density. Handy for placeholder objects in scenes destined for real-time or print output.

name: MeshCylinder
description: Creates a cylinder as a polygon mesh. Used where lightweight faceted geometry is preferable to NURBS, such as context models.

name: MeshCone
description: Creates a cone as a polygon mesh. A quick faceted primitive for context and export models.

name: MeshTorus
description: Creates a ring as a polygon mesh. Occasionally useful for faceted loops in visualisation scenes.

name: MeshPlane
description: Creates a rectangular mesh plane with a set grid of faces. A common base for terrain sculpting and drape-style studies in mesh workflows.

name: ReduceMesh
description: Lowers a mesh's polygon count while preserving its shape as far as possible. Essential for taming scan data and dense downloads before they slow the model.

name: Weld
description: Merges coincident mesh vertices within an angle tolerance so faces share smooth shading. Fixes faceted-looking seams on imported meshes.

name: Unweld
description: Splits mesh vertices along edges above a crease angle so those edges shade as sharp. Used to restore crisp arris lines on smoothed meshes.

name: UnweldEdge
description: Unwelds only the specific mesh edges you pick, making them shade as creases. Precise control over which lines read sharp in a rendered mesh.

name: UnifyMeshNormals
description: Flips inconsistent face normals so the whole mesh points one way. A standard repair before boolean operations, rendering or 3D printing.

name: FillMeshHole
description: Caps a single naked hole in a mesh with new faces. Quick patching during mesh repair for printing or rendering.

name: FillMeshHoles
description: Caps every closed naked border in a mesh in one pass. The bulk version of FillMeshHole for making scans watertight.

name: MatchMeshEdge
description: Moves mesh vertices so neighbouring naked edges line up and close small gaps. Used when separate mesh parts almost meet but leave hairline cracks.

name: MeshRepair
description: Opens a guided panel that checks a mesh and walks through fixing its defects step by step. The first stop when a downloaded or scanned mesh refuses to print or boolean.

name: MeshBooleanUnion
description: Merges overlapping closed meshes into a single mesh. The mesh counterpart to BooleanUnion for print-ready models.

name: MeshBooleanDifference
description: Subtracts one set of closed meshes from another. Used to cut openings in scan or export meshes without converting to NURBS.

name: MeshBooleanIntersection
description: Keeps only the shared volume of intersecting closed meshes. Handy for clash volumes and trimming context meshes to a site boundary.

name: MeshBooleanSplit
description: Splits meshes into parts along their mutual intersections, keeping all pieces. Useful for dividing terrain meshes along plot boundaries.

name: MeshSplit
description: Splits a mesh with curves, surfaces or other meshes without needing closed volumes. The general-purpose divider for open meshes like terrain.

name: MeshTrim
description: Cuts away the picked side of a mesh along a curve or surface. Everyday tool for trimming site meshes to boundaries.

name: MeshOutline
description: Draws the outline of a mesh as seen from the current view as a planar curve. Great for site plan silhouettes of context models and quick shadow footprints.

name: MeshToNURB
description: Converts every mesh face into a NURBS surface joined as a polysurface. A blunt but effective route when downstream tools demand NURBS, best kept for small meshes.

name: ExtractMeshFaces
description: Detaches selected faces from a mesh into a separate mesh object. Used to isolate a roof plane or facade zone from a context scan.

name: ExtractMeshPart
description: Pulls out one connected region of a disjoint mesh as its own object. Quick way to separate buildings merged into a single downloaded city mesh.

name: SplitDisjointMesh
description: Breaks a mesh containing unconnected pieces into separate mesh objects. The bulk version of ExtractMeshPart for cleaning imported models.

name: DeleteMeshFaces
description: Removes picked faces from a mesh, leaving holes. Used to strip unwanted clutter such as scan noise, cars or vegetation from context meshes.

name: TriangulateMesh
description: Splits all quad mesh faces into triangles. Required by some export formats and analysis tools that only accept triangulated geometry.

name: QuadrangulateMesh
description: Merges pairs of triangles into quads where they lie close to planar. Tidies triangulated meshes into cleaner, lighter topology.

name: ShrinkWrap
description: Wraps a watertight mesh tightly around any collection of geometry, meshes or point clouds. A Rhino 8 favourite for turning messy scans and mixed models into a single printable solid mesh.

name: Flip
description: Reverses the direction of curves, or the normals of surfaces and meshes. Fixes offsets going the wrong way and dark, inside-out faces in renders.

name: Move
description: Moves objects from a base point to a target point with full snapping precision. The most fundamental transform, preferred over dragging when accuracy matters.

name: Copy
description: Duplicates objects from a base point to one or more target points. The everyday tool for repeating elements around a drawing with precision.

name: Rotate
description: Rotates objects around a centre point within the construction plane. Constant companion for orienting plans, furniture and site elements.

name: Rotate3D
description: Rotates objects around an axis you define by two points in space. Needed whenever the rotation is out of the construction plane, like tilting a roof panel.

name: Scale
description: Resizes objects uniformly in all directions from an origin, by factor or reference distance. Used to correct imported drawing scales and resize elements proportionally.

name: Scale1D
description: Stretches objects along a single direction only. Ideal for lengthening a table, corridor or facade bay without changing its other proportions.

name: Scale2D
description: Scales objects in two directions while holding the third. Useful for resizing plans in plan-only without altering heights.

name: ScaleNU
description: Scales objects by independent factors along X, Y and Z. The tool for squashing or stretching massing studies non-uniformly.

name: Mirror
description: Reflects objects across a line or plane, optionally keeping the original. Essential for symmetrical plans, handed apartment types and reflected details.

name: Symmetry
description: Mirrors a curve or SubD edge across a plane and keeps the join smooth, with history so edits stay symmetrical. Used for precise symmetrical design curves and SubD halves.

name: Array
description: Copies objects into a rectangular grid with set counts and spacing in X, Y and Z. The base tool for column grids, seating layouts and repeated bays.

name: ArrayLinear
description: Copies objects repeatedly along a single direction at even spacing. Quick for fence posts, joists and any one-directional rhythm.

name: ArrayPolar
description: Copies objects around a centre point through a set angle and count. The go-to for radial structures, stair balusters on a curve and circular seating.

name: ArrayCrv
description: Copies objects along a curve by count or spacing, optionally rotating them to follow it. Perfect for balustrades, ribs and streetlights along a curved route.

name: ArraySrf
description: Copies an object across a surface in its U and V directions, orienting each copy to the surface normal. The manual panelisation tool for cladding studies and facade components.

name: ArrayCrvOnSrf
description: Copies objects along a curve that lies on a surface, keeping each copy normal to the surface. Used for fixings or fins that must track a curved seam on a facade.

name: Orient
description: Moves, rotates and optionally scales objects by mapping two reference points onto two targets. A compound transform that places elements in one action instead of three.

name: Orient3Pt
description: Repositions objects by matching three reference points to three targets, fixing position and orientation in space. The reliable way to place a component onto a sloping plane.

name: OrientOnSrf
description: Places copies of an object onto a surface, aligned to the surface normal at each pick. Great for scattering rooflights or fixings across curved geometry by eye.

name: OrientOnCrv
description: Places objects along a curve, orienting each to the curve direction. Useful for positioning individual elements like bollards where regular array spacing will not do.

name: RemapCPlane
description: Re-orients objects from one construction plane to another, as if the geometry were drawn on the new plane. Excellent for moving 2D details onto sloped or vertical faces.

name: Flow
description: Re-shapes objects from along a straight base curve onto a target curve, bending them to follow it. The classic trick for modelling straight, then curving the result along a path.

name: FlowAlongSrf
description: Maps objects from a flat base surface onto a target surface, morphing them to its curvature. The standard route for applying panel systems and patterns designed flat onto doubly curved facades.

name: Splop
description: Copies and morphs an object from a plane onto a surface at picked points, with rotate and scale control while placing. Fun and fast for stamping repeated ornaments over curved forms.

name: Sporph
description: Morphs objects from one surface's parameter space to another's, deforming them between the two shapes. Used to migrate detailed geometry between design iterations of a surface.

name: Bend
description: Bends objects along a spine between two points, with control over the arc. Useful for curving straight elements like trusses or louvres through an angle.

name: Twist
description: Rotates an object progressively along an axis so it spirals between start and end angles. The instant twisted-tower and helical-fin tool.

name: Taper
description: Scales an object progressively along an axis so it narrows or widens towards one end. Quick way to give massing a tapering silhouette.

name: Stretch
description: Elongates only the middle region of objects along an axis, leaving the ends undistorted. Ideal for lengthening a chair rail or window while keeping its end details intact.

name: Shear
description: Slants objects at an angle while keeping their base fixed. Used for leaning facades, italic-style extrusions and racking studies.

name: Maelstrom
description: Spirals objects around an axis so they whirl progressively with radius. A specialist deformer for vortex-like patterns and twisted radial compositions.

name: SoftMove
description: Moves geometry or control points with a smooth falloff from a centre, like a soft magnet. Useful for organic nudges to terrain and sculpted surfaces.

name: CageEdit
description: Surrounds objects with a low-point control cage and deforms them by moving its points. The heavyweight freeform editor for reshaping whole buildings or complex assemblies smoothly.

name: Cage
description: Creates a standalone box, line or surface cage object for later use with CageEdit. Set up once, then reuse across multiple deformation studies.

name: SetPt
description: Flattens selected objects or control points to a shared X, Y or Z value. The classic tool for levelling points onto a datum, such as zeroing survey linework to Z0.

name: ProjectToCPlane
description: Squashes objects flat onto the construction plane, optionally keeping the originals. Instantly turns 3D linework into a true 2D plan underlay.

name: Align
description: Lines up selected objects by their edges or centres, vertically or horizontally. Tidies drawing layouts and rows of objects without manual snapping.

name: Distribute
description: Spaces selected objects evenly between the outermost ones along an axis. Companion to Align for tidy elevation compositions and furniture rows.

name: Gumball
description: Toggles the on-object widget that drags, rotates and scales selections along its arrows and arcs, with extrude and copy modifiers. Most designers leave it on as their primary hands-on transform tool.

name: Drag
description: Sets how click-and-drag moving behaves, including CPlane or view-based dragging. Worth knowing when dragged objects jump to unexpected planes in 3D views.

name: Trim
description: Cuts away the parts of objects you click, using other objects as cutting edges. Together with Split and Join, the core editing operation in every Rhino session.

name: Split
description: Divides objects into pieces where cutters cross them, keeping every part. Preferred over Trim when you want to recolour, move or keep both sides of a cut.

name: Join
description: Connects touching curves into polycurves, or surfaces into polysurfaces and closed solids. The glue command used constantly to assemble edited geometry back together.

name: Explode
description: Breaks joined objects into their component curves, surfaces or mesh parts, and dissolves blocks and groups of segments. First step whenever a compound object needs part-by-part editing.

name: Rebuild
description: Reconstructs curves or surfaces with a chosen degree and control point count, evening out their structure. Standard clean-up before matching, deforming or exporting geometry.

name: ChangeDegree
description: Raises or lowers the polynomial degree of a curve or surface, adding or reducing flexibility. Used when geometry needs more subtle shaping or simpler structure for matching.

name: Undo
description: Steps back through recent commands, reversing changes to the model. The most pressed shortcut in any session.

name: Redo
description: Reinstates the last change that Undo reversed. Handy when you step back one change too far.

name: Delete
description: Removes the selected objects from the model. Paired with the Sel commands for fast bulk clean-ups.

name: Cut
description: Removes the selection and places it on the clipboard for pasting, including into another open Rhino file. Standard clipboard workflow between models.

name: CopyToClipboard
description: Copies the selection to the clipboard without removing it, ready to paste in place or into another file. The quickest way to shuttle geometry between open models.

name: Paste
description: Places clipboard contents into the model at their original coordinates. Completes the cut and copy clipboard workflow across files.

name: PointsOn
description: Displays the control points of curves and surfaces so they can be dragged directly. The doorway into hands-on NURBS editing.

name: PointsOff
description: Hides control points when direct editing is finished. Prevents accidental dragging of points while working nearby.

name: History
description: Controls recording of parent-child links so edits to input curves update dependent surfaces automatically. Powerful for iterative design where profiles keep changing after lofts and sweeps are built.

name: Properties
description: Opens the panel showing the selected object's layer, colour, material and type-specific settings. The everyday place to check and adjust what something is.

name: MatchProperties
description: Copies display and object properties such as layer, colour and linetype from one object to others. Fast way to bring rogue imports in line with your drawing standards.

name: Layer
description: Opens the layers panel to create, rename, colour and structure layers and sublayers. The heart of model organisation in every professional Rhino file.

name: ChangeLayer
description: Moves selected objects onto a different layer chosen from a list. Quicker than the properties panel for bulk re-layering during clean-ups.

name: OneLayerOn
description: Turns on a single chosen layer and switches every other layer off. Instant focus when auditing one system, such as structure only.

name: LayerStateManager
description: Saves and restores named combinations of layer visibility, colour and locking. Lets one model serve many outputs, like planning drawings versus detail packages.

name: Group
description: Binds selected objects into a group that selects as one. Light-touch organisation for furniture sets and repeated assemblies that do not warrant a block.

name: Ungroup
description: Dissolves the selected group back into independent objects. The exit route when grouped items need separate editing.

name: AddToGroup
description: Adds extra objects into an existing group without rebuilding it. Keeps evolving assemblies tidy as elements are added.

name: RemoveFromGroup
description: Takes selected objects out of their group while leaving the rest grouped. Useful for promoting one element out of a set for separate treatment.

name: Block
description: Defines selected geometry as a named block so copies insert as lightweight linked instances. Editing the definition updates every instance, ideal for repeated windows, furniture and units.

name: Insert
description: Places an instance of a block definition, or an external file as a block, at a chosen point and scale. The entry point for component-based and referenced modelling.

name: BlockManager
description: Lists every block definition in the file with counts, links and update controls. The housekeeping hub for models built on components and externally referenced files.

name: BlockEdit
description: Opens a block definition for editing in place, with surrounding context shown. Changes propagate to every instance on exit, keeping repeated elements consistent.

name: Hide
description: Makes selected objects invisible without deleting them. Constant tool for decluttering the view while working on something behind or inside.

name: Show
description: Reveals all hidden objects at once. The blanket undo for a session's worth of hiding.

name: ShowSelected
description: Temporarily displays hidden objects so you can pick which ones to reveal, leaving the rest hidden. Precision control when only some hidden items should return.

name: Lock
description: Makes selected objects visible but unselectable, greyed in the viewport. Perfect for reference geometry and context you must see but never nudge.

name: Unlock
description: Releases all locked objects so they can be selected again. Blanket partner to Lock.

name: UnlockSelected
description: Lets you pick specific locked objects to release while others stay locked. Fine-grained partner to Unlock for busy reference-heavy files.

name: Isolate
description: Hides everything except the selected objects in one step. The fastest way to focus on a single element inside a dense model.

name: Unisolate
description: Restores the objects hidden by the last Isolate. Returns the full model after focused work.

name: SelAll
description: Selects every visible, unlocked object in the model. Common first step before bulk transforms, exports or clean-ups.

name: SelNone
description: Clears the current selection entirely. Useful in scripts and when Escape is mapped elsewhere.

name: Invert
description: Swaps the selection to everything currently unselected. Handy trick: select what you want to keep, invert, then hide or delete the rest.

name: SelCrv
description: Selects all curve objects in one hit. Ideal for bulk operations like moving construction linework to its own layer.

name: SelSrf
description: Selects every single-surface object in the model. Useful for separating unjoined surfaces from finished polysurfaces during clean-ups.

name: SelPolysrf
description: Selects all polysurfaces, including closed solids. Quick filter when exporting or re-layering built massing.

name: SelMesh
description: Selects all mesh objects. Convenient for isolating imported context meshes from native NURBS work.

name: SelSubD
description: Selects all SubD objects in the model. Useful when converting or re-layering sculpted concept geometry en masse.

name: SelPt
description: Selects every point object. Typical use is deleting leftover setting-out or divide points before issuing a model.

name: SelDup
description: Selects objects that are exact duplicates sitting on top of others. The classic pre-delete step for cleaning files bloated by double geometry.

name: SelLast
description: Reselects the objects changed or created by the most recent command. Invaluable for chaining operations, like moving what you just imported.

name: SelPrev
description: Restores the previous selection set. A lifesaver after accidentally deselecting a painstaking multi-pick.

name: SelLayer
description: Selects every object on layers you choose. Combines with hide, export or transform commands for layer-wide operations.

name: SelColor
description: Selects all objects displaying a chosen colour. Useful for rounding up imports whose colours came in by object rather than layer.

name: SelChain
description: Selects a run of curves or edges connected end to end from one pick. Speeds up choosing rails and boundaries for sweeps, lofts and fillets.

name: SelSmall
description: Selects objects smaller than a size you give. Excellent for catching slivers and debris left over from trims and imports.

name: SelName
description: Selects objects by their assigned object name. Depends on disciplined naming, but then gives instant pinpoint selection in large files.

name: Dim
description: Places a horizontal or vertical linear dimension between two points. The bread-and-butter dimensioning tool for plans and elevations.

name: DimAligned
description: Places a dimension parallel to the line between its two picked points. Used for measuring along sloped walls, stairs and raked elements.

name: DimRotated
description: Places a linear dimension at a set angle regardless of the picked points' alignment. Useful for dimensioning against a rotated grid or datum.

name: DimAngle
description: Dimensions the angle between two lines or three points with an arc leader. Standard for splayed walls and angled setting-out.

name: DimRadius
description: Annotates the radius of an arc or circle with a leadered value. Essential on setting-out drawings for curved kerbs, walls and fillets.

name: DimDiameter
description: Annotates the diameter of a circle or arc. Preferred over radius for holes, penetrations and circular components.

name: DimOrdinate
description: Places running X or Y coordinate dimensions from a datum origin. Common on fabrication and setting-out drawings where chains of dimensions would clutter.

name: DimCurveLength
description: Annotates the true developed length of a curve rather than a straight distance. Useful for handrails, cable runs and curved facades where arc length matters.

name: Leader
description: Draws an arrowed leader line with attached text. The standard tool for calling up notes against specific parts of a drawing.

name: Text
description: Places a block of annotation text at a picked point, styled by the current annotation style. Used for titles, notes and labels throughout drawings.

name: TextObject
description: Generates real geometry from text as curves, surfaces or solids. Reach for it for signage, embossed lettering and CNC-cut graphics rather than annotation.

name: Hatch
description: Fills closed boundaries with a pattern or solid fill. Brings plans and sections up to drawing standard with material and poche indication.

name: Centermark
description: Places a centre cross on an arc or circle. Small but essential drafting mark for setting out circular elements.

name: RevCloud
description: Draws a revision cloud around areas of change on a drawing. Added in Rhino 8 to support standard drawing issue and mark-up conventions.

name: Make2D
description: Generates flat 2D line drawings of the model from a view, with hidden lines on separate layers. The bridge from 3D model to plans, sections and elevations for drafting.

name: Layout
description: Creates a paper-space page with a title-block-ready sheet and viewports onto the model. The starting point for issuing scaled, printable drawings straight from Rhino.

name: Detail
description: Adds and manages viewport windows on a layout page, each with its own view and scale. Used to compose plans, elevations and 3D views on one sheet.

name: Print
description: Sends layouts or viewports to a printer or PDF with scale, line width and colour controls. The final step in issuing drawings from Rhino.

name: Distance
description: Reports the distance between two picked points. The quickest sanity check on clearances and spacings while modelling.

name: Length
description: Reports the true length of curves and edges. Used for quantities such as handrail runs, skirting lengths and cable routes.

name: Angle
description: Measures the angle between two lines or defined directions. Companion to Distance for checking splays and slopes.

name: Radius
description: Reports the radius of a curve at a picked point. Quick verification that curved elements meet minimum bend or turning radii.

name: Area
description: Calculates the area of closed curves, hatches, surfaces or meshes. Constantly used for schedules of accommodation and material take-offs.

name: AreaCentroid
description: Calculates area and marks the centroid with a point. Useful for balance points in structural sketches and for centring elements within outlines.

name: Volume
description: Calculates the enclosed volume of closed solids or meshes. Key for cut-and-fill studies, concrete quantities and capacity checks.

name: VolumeCentroid
description: Finds the centre of mass of closed volumes and marks it with a point. Used in stability and rigging studies for heavy elements.

name: BoundingBox
description: Draws the smallest world- or CPlane-aligned box enclosing the selection. Handy for overall envelope dimensions, crate sizing and stock material checks.

name: Dir
description: Displays and edits the direction arrows of curves and the normals of surfaces or meshes. First diagnostic when offsets, extrusions or textures behave back to front.

name: CurvatureGraph
description: Displays comb-like graphs showing how curvature varies along curves and surface edges. The professional's tool for judging whether a curve is genuinely fair before surfacing.

name: CurvatureAnalysis
description: Shades surfaces with false colour showing Gaussian or mean curvature. Reveals flat spots, dents and double curvature that plain shading hides.

name: Zebra
description: Projects stripe patterns onto surfaces so continuity flaws show as kinked or broken stripes. The quickest visual check of how smoothly surfaces meet.

name: EMap
description: Reflects a chosen environment image in the model's surfaces as a quality check. Simulates how a polished or glazed finish will reveal surface defects.

name: DraftAngleAnalysis
description: Colours surfaces by their angle from a pull direction. Used to check mould release on cast components and to map facade panels against rain or solar angle thresholds.

name: ThicknessAnalysis
description: Colour-maps the wall thickness of closed solids or meshes between set limits. Valuable for checking shelled components and 3D print walls before fabrication.

name: EdgeContinuity
description: Displays live position, tangency and curvature deviation between two selected edges. A focused matching diagnostic introduced alongside modern surfacing tools in Rhino 7.

name: ShowEdges
description: Highlights the edges of surfaces and meshes, with naked and non-manifold edges picked out in colour. The go-to diagnostic when a join fails or a solid will not close.

name: PointDeviation
description: Measures and colour-codes how far a set of points sits from a surface or mesh. Used to verify a rebuilt surface against original scan data.

name: CrvDeviation
description: Reports the minimum and maximum distance between two curves. Useful for checking a simplified curve against its source or clearances between routes.

name: EvaluatePt
description: Reports the exact world or CPlane coordinates of a picked point. Everyday check for setting-out values and datum levels.

name: What
description: Prints a detailed report of an object's type, structure and validity. First stop for identifying mystery geometry in inherited files.

name: List
description: Dumps the full internal data structure of an object, down to knots and control points. A deep debugging tool for advanced users and developers.

name: Check
description: Tests selected objects for internal errors and reports whether they are valid. Routine health check before booleans, exports and file handovers.

name: SelBadObjects
description: Selects every invalid object in the model in one command. Pairs with Check to locate and repair or replace corrupt geometry.

name: ExtractBadSrf
description: Pulls the invalid faces out of polysurfaces so they can be repaired or rebuilt in isolation. Surgical follow-up to SelBadObjects on complex models.

name: Zoom
description: Zooms the viewport by window, extents, selected objects or factor. Its aliases make framing the whole model or a selection a two-keystroke habit.

name: Pan
description: Slides the view across the model without changing zoom or angle. Basic navigation alongside Zoom and view rotation.

name: RotateView
description: Orbits the camera around the view target. The keyboard-driven counterpart to right-mouse orbiting in perspective views.

name: RotateCamera
description: Swivels the camera in place, like turning your head rather than orbiting the model. Useful for interior views where the eye position must stay fixed.

name: Walkabout
description: Moves the camera at eye level with walking-style controls. Handy for checking interior spatial experience without setting up a full walkthrough.

name: Plan
description: Sets the viewport to look straight down at the current construction plane. Instant return to true plan after working in 3D.

name: SetView
description: Points the viewport at a standard direction such as Top, Front, Right or Perspective, in world or CPlane terms. The command behind the standard view buttons.

name: 4View
description: Restores the classic four-viewport arrangement of Top, Front, Right and Perspective. Quick reset when viewport layouts get into a muddle.

name: NamedView
description: Saves and restores camera positions by name, with thumbnails. Essential for repeatable render views and keeping agreed verified-view camera setups.

name: NewFloatingViewport
description: Opens an extra viewport in its own window, ideal for a second monitor. Lets you keep a render view open while drafting in another.

name: MaxViewport
description: Toggles the active viewport between maximised and the multi-view layout. Usually driven by double-clicking the viewport title.

name: OneView
description: Runs a single-viewport mode that swaps the construction plane automatically as you orbit near standard directions. A drafting-friendly way to work in one big view.

name: Shade
description: Temporarily displays the viewport shaded regardless of its display mode. A quick look at form and shadow while staying in wireframe workflows.

name: SetDisplayMode
description: Switches the viewport between display modes such as Wireframe, Shaded, Rendered, Ghosted, Arctic and Raytraced. Different modes suit drafting, design review and presentation checking.

name: CPlane
description: Redefines the construction plane by origin, three points, object or view. Mastering CPlanes is the key to drawing accurately on sloped roofs and angled facades.

name: NamedCPlane
description: Saves and restores construction planes by name. Keeps a library of working planes for each facade, roof pitch or datum in a project.

name: AutoCPlane
description: Automatically aligns the construction plane to whatever object or face you select. A Rhino 8 quality-of-life tool that removes constant manual CPlane setting when detailing angled geometry.

name: ClippingPlane
description: Places a plane that cuts the viewport display away on one side, revealing a live section. Invaluable for working inside buildings and presenting sectional 3D views.

name: SectionStyles
description: Controls how clipped geometry displays at the cut, including hatch, fill and edge styling per object or layer. Part of the Rhino 8 sectioning workflow for drawing-quality live sections.

name: Turntable
description: Spins the model continuously in the viewport. A simple way to review a design from all sides or run an impromptu presentation loop.

name: Fullscreen
description: Expands the viewport to fill the screen, hiding interface panels. Ideal for design reviews and client presentations without leaving Rhino.

name: ViewCaptureToFile
description: Saves an image of the viewport at chosen resolution, with options for grid and widget visibility. The workhorse for quick design-study images without full rendering.

name: ViewCaptureToClipboard
description: Copies a viewport image straight to the clipboard for pasting into emails, decks and documents. The fastest route from model to meeting note.

name: Camera
description: Shows or hides the active view's camera widget so its position, target and lens can be manipulated as objects. Used to fine-tune verified views and match photographs.

name: Grid
description: Adjusts the construction plane grid's extents, spacing and snap intervals. Worth setting early so the grid matches your project's planning module.

name: UndoView
description: Steps back through recent view changes without touching geometry. Rescues you after an accidental zoom or orbit loses a carefully framed view.

name: Ortho
description: Toggles constraint of cursor movement to set angle increments, typically 90 degrees. Fundamental drafting aid for keeping lines square.

name: Osnap
description: Opens the object snap controls for end, mid, centre, intersection and other precise picks. Accurate modelling in Rhino lives and dies by these snaps.

name: Snapshots
description: Saves named states combining view, layer visibility, object states and more, with animated transitions between them. Powerful for presenting design options and phasing from one model.

name: New
description: Starts a fresh model from a template that sets units and tolerances. Choosing the right template avoids tolerance headaches later.

name: Open
description: Opens a Rhino model or any of the many supported CAD and mesh formats. Alongside Import, the gateway for consultant and manufacturer files.

name: Save
description: Saves the current model, including its render meshes and previews. Frequent saving plus IncrementalSave is cheap insurance on live projects.

name: SaveAs
description: Saves the model under a new name, location or earlier Rhino version. Also the route to handing files to consultants on older releases.

name: SaveSmall
description: Saves without render meshes to produce a much smaller file. Standard practice before emailing or archiving large models.

name: IncrementalSave
description: Saves a numbered copy each time it runs, building a version trail. A lightweight manual version control habit for design development.

name: Revert
description: Abandons unsaved changes and reloads the file from disk. The emergency exit after an experiment goes wrong beyond comfortable undoing.

name: Import
description: Brings geometry from another file into the current model, converting from formats like DWG, IGES, STEP, SKP and OBJ. The daily bridge to consultant and product data.

name: Export
description: Writes the selected objects out to another file and format. Used constantly to issue geometry to consultants, fabricators and other software.

name: ExportWithOrigin
description: Exports selected objects with a picked base point that becomes the new file's origin. Vital for keeping shared coordinates sane when exchanging fragments of large site models.

name: Worksession
description: Attaches other Rhino files as read-only references around your active file, so a team can split a big project into parts. Rhino's answer to external references for large-project collaboration.

name: Audit
description: Checks the open model's database for errors and reports what it finds. Run with Purge and SaveSmall as a standard file hygiene routine.

name: Purge
description: Deletes unused layers, blocks, materials and other invisible data bloating the file. Often reclaims dramatic file size on long-running project models.

name: Options
description: Opens Rhino's global settings for display, toolbars, aliases, modelling aids and more. Where you tune the environment to your own working style.

name: DocumentProperties
description: Opens settings that belong to the current file, such as units, tolerances, grid and annotation styles. Getting tolerances right here prevents most downstream joining and boolean grief.

name: Notes
description: Opens a simple text panel stored inside the model file. Useful for issue notes, modelling conventions and handover instructions that travel with the file.

name: CommandHistory
description: Opens the scrolling log of recent commands and their reported results. Where you retrieve measurement outputs and diagnose what a command actually did.

name: Picture
description: Places an image in the model as a picture plane, commonly used to trace scanned drawings or display reference imagery. Successor to the old PictureFrame command.

name: PackageManager
description: Browses, installs and updates plug-ins and resources from the official package server. The modern route to extending Rhino with tools like section utilities and renderers.

name: Render
description: Renders the current view with the active renderer into the render window. The starting point for presentation images beyond viewport captures.

name: Sun
description: Controls a sun light by date, time and location for accurate shadows. Essential for daylight and rights-of-light style studies directly in the viewport.

name: SystemInfo
description: Prints a report of Rhino's version, graphics hardware and loaded plug-ins. The first thing support asks for when troubleshooting display or stability issues.

name: Grasshopper
description: Opens Grasshopper, Rhino's visual programming environment for parametric and generative design. The centre of computational workflows from facade panelisation to environmental studies.

name: GrasshopperPlayer
description: Runs a Grasshopper definition as if it were a native command, prompting for inputs without opening the canvas. Lets teams share parametric tools with colleagues who never touch Grasshopper.
